steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Alright. We should be safe here.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Cador, it's still a mess outside. We're most certainly not in Londinium anymore. I reckon we can see the situation outside the plate from the top of the old loading tower, but I can't get near it. It's outside the restricted area.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: And I reckon even if you could spot anything, it wouldn't mean a thing. The Sarkaz keep a close eye, and... there are too many of them.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: And what's the old bloke's story?

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Hmph, he was trying to talk terms with the Sarkaz?

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: And how did that turn out?

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Take a look yourself.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: There. That's about all I can do, bandaging your wound.

steps.name: Timid Citizen
steps.text: Thank... Thank you.

steps.name: Timid Citizen
steps.text: Goodness... Why... Just what happened?

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: What else could've happened? The Sarkaz have been in Londinium for four years now.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: You can't possibly still think they were invited here by that poor sod Cavendish as his guests, right?

steps.name: Timid Citizen
steps.text: But they haven't ever...

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Haven't ever what?

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: You must be one of those noblemen who never leave their mansions and need their maids to fetch them their morning cystymilk. How'd you fall so low as to find yourself in Norport?

steps.name: Timid Citizen
steps.text: No, no, I'm but a scholar. I have merely run into certain... troubles financially. As soon as I finish my manuscript, I shall...

steps.name: Timid Citizen
steps.text: Drat! The manuscript is still in my study!

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Baird, you've really got a knack for finding these poor, down-on-their-luck bastards, don't you?

steps.name: Timid Citizen
steps.text: Would you at least have some respect? If all goes well, it's very likely I will become the Royal Academy of Sciences' next academician!

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: 'Very likely.' Heh.

steps.name: Timid Citizen
steps.text: I still don't understand. The news kept saying that...

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: 'All is well.' What more do you want them to say? 'Friends and citizens, I sincerely regret to inform you that Londinium is now a shithole?'

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: The 'special instructors' that they sent to the newspaper offices and TV stations actually earned their keep, you know?

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Did you see whose flag they're flying above the munitions factory in Highbury? If not, you've got to at least remember the fire in Auchterigg the other day, right?

steps.name: Timid Citizen
steps.text: But the war... What about the Defense Forces? The dukes? Aren't they defending us all around Londinium?

steps.name: Timid Citizen
steps.text: How can this be...? The Sarkaz can't possibly triumph over the dukes, can they? The devils are a bunch of savages who cower in the wilderness, but Victoria is the greatest country across all the lands!

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Who told you that? Did you realize that out of nowhere while munching on cake at home?

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: I didn't feel that way at all when the dibbles held me up against the wall and frisked me.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Alright, 'Next Academician,' off you go. You don't belong here.

steps.name: Timid Citizen
steps.text: But... where can I go?

steps.name: Timid Citizen
steps.text: My flat is not in this lockdown zone, and I haven't the slightest idea where my loyal servant is... I know no one here.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Tch.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: What can you do? Medical work, sewing, repair, anything.

steps.name: Timid Citizen
steps.text: M-My research is in heraldry...

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: You scholarly chaps ever studied how to turn air into steaks?

steps.name: Timid Citizen
steps.text: Well... it is by no means my area of expertise, but I'd imagine it's a little difficult...

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Baird, stop bringing these fancy lads back, will ya? He doesn't even understand sarcasm.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: We don't have a lot of supplies on hand here.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: *sigh*... Maybe he can help Delphine manage the warehouse?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Baird! Stop trying to pass all your problems to me!

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: I can't very well watch him die on the street.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: At times like this, we have to come together and unite as one. Even having one extra man on board is more power to us.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: 'Come together...' *sigh*.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I wish Parliament and the dukes would learn from you people. We wouldn't have fallen to where we are today.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: You think they're not united enough? They were all very united when it came to hanging the king.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: That was... *sigh*, never mind.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I just hope you'll be of some use, Mr. 'Next Academician.'

steps.name: Timid Citizen
steps.text: I shall do everything in my power! Though, speaking of which... who would all of you be?

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Who are we?

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Alright, welcome to our gym, the 'Slobberknocker'!

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: You can call us Glasgow.

a.text: To tell the truth, I haven't any idea where you have been as of late. Ever since Mr. Adams the bookshop owner died, I haven't been able to reach you.
It has been a long time since I last continued our work.
Forgive me, my dear friend. I never hide anything from you.
But I am truly very... befuddled.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: You once told me that peace would come again...

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: But I can't fool myself with false hope anymore. I can't hide in my room and pretend that everything we do is still meaningful.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Right, we could look at things on a broader scale. 'The dimension of history...'

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Of course, peace will come. It will, eventually.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: And war will undoubtedly shatter it in an even crueler way.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I once thought we could win, and I still hope that we will win.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: But, Heidi, if everything that we have done amounts to nothing but self-comfort...

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: No, not 'if.' This might already be the truth...

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: These books, these desks, and this school that may come crumbling down at any moment... How are they meant to stand up against the force of a new era?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Heidi, I can't... I can't keep going anymore.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: What should I do?

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Lady Golding, are you alright?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Molly... you're back.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Are you writing a letter?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: No, this is nothing.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I... I just remembered a few novels that I read before.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: The protagonists are always charming, suave, always heading to the frontlines wearing a uniform befitting of them with a pipe in their mouths.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: But the authors never tell us which battlefield they head to and how the trenches smell.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Those who are enamored of the protagonist, both women and men, taste fine desserts with anxious hearts—

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Of course, we all know these are just literary techniques. The stories always end happily.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Authors with a little bit of ambition might try to build what the critics call a 'profound' atmosphere.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: The stories are adorned with preventable deaths, and they are always the protagonist's comrade and dearest friend, dying in the trenches to shield the hero.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: In the end, the wretched enemy finds themselves defeated by the hero's sword, thus restoring justice and morality.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: And at his fallen friend's funeral, a solemn crowd gathers to remember his heroics, as petals symbolizing honor are scattered atop the casket.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: This is the most emotional part. The protagonist clenches his fist, wipes his tears, and looks toward the morning sun with resolve—

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: And without fail, they always say that hope will come and all sacrifices will be meaningful.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: And there. That's where the author stops. Let the readers imagine for themselves that truly beautiful future. Let them bask in that stately feeling in the end.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: I'm surprised you read these kinds of novels.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: It was years ago. Everyone was that age once.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I used to be obsessed with these books when I was still a young girl... I wasn't very attached to the protagonists, actually, but I was indeed obsessed with those deaths.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Sometimes, I imagined myself one of those heroes who sacrificed themselves for their cause, and the masses would sing my praises for the era I helped create or, at the very least, my sacrifice...

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Hah. How childish.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Later on, I thought I'd be clear-headed enough to see past these sugar-coated fantasies.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: But then... I started to notice... there might be nothing inherently different between who I am now and who I was back then.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Don't say that. You told the children yourself. Death is a solemn topic.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Hah, did I? I don't remember.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Perhaps it was just the lectures that I've got so used to giving.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: How was procurement today?

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Not too bad. The situation on the streets isn't very serious. The prices at the shops haven't gone up, though there were more city defense soldiers than usual, and the Sarkaz solders... they're not as secretive they used to be.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: But everyone is pretending as if nothing has happened. Except... what used to be Norport. There is nothing left except the support structures extending from the surrounding districts.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: What about those places?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I need to apologize to you again. I should never have dragged you into this. It's just... Lettou has his eyes on me, and every time I step out the door, I find myself followed by several ill-meaning men.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I had no choice but to make a gamble—that you are not on their watchlist yet.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: No, I'm glad to do my part for Londinium.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: It's just that the places you told me about were all pretty quiet. I used the passwords, but no one answered.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Maybe... Maybe they've already given up?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: No, they are all stronger than I am. Much stronger.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: But I've found a letter. It should be for you, so I didn't open it.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: This... No, this isn't their handwriting.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: The letter has practically all the information on the Self-Salvation Corps' communications.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: What?! But... how could that...?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: This is a threat.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: They... They know us like the back of their hand.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Then... What should we do, Lady Golding?!

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Molly, I'll have another list of places for you.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I've never been to these bases myself, but having analyzed the flow of information... they should be there.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I shouldn't take this risk. This goes against our established practices, but...

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: This information is important to the Self-Salvation Corps, right?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Many lives are on the line.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Then we must do this.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Molly... Just as I taught you, watch out for anyone who could be tailing you. Whether they are Sarkaz or not, do not let your guard down.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Look for a girl called Clovisia there or anyone who can get in contact with her. Tell them that the entire intelligence network has been exposed. They must evacuate immediately!

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Lady Golding, where are you going?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: To Lettou's office.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I will try to buy as much time as I can for the rest of you.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: But—

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Relax, I'll be fine. I...

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I just hope I'm stronger than I think I am.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor, I had a dream.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I saw... the city shrouded in dark clouds, and bloodstained Sarkaz flags flew above every building. Outside the city... Originium grew everywhere my eyes could see.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I saw a rusted throne towering above the lands. The masses kneeled before it, crying tears stained in black. I saw the person on the throne wave their arm, and the shouts that followed pierced the sky.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Yet, in the shadow of the throne, the cowering men lifted their heads ever so slightly...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I felt what they felt...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I don't know how to describe it... It was so all over the place, so stifled...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I could only make out what was on the surface. That pain...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...and hatred.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Who was that on the throne...?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Is this the future that the collective souls of the Sarkaz foresaw? Or is this... the duty of the King of Sarkaz?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Did Theresa have this dream? Could this be... the sights she is looking forward to now?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: No, it can't be.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor, this dream... It doesn't mean anything, right?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Thank you, Doctor.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Right, it was... just a dream...

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Amiya, Doctor.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Is Dr. Kal'tsit better?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Hard to say. Her body... was frail to start with, and her wounds are deep.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Shining has attempted several solutions, but all of them were limited in their effectiveness. She has yet to awaken.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Mon3tr seems to be slowly repairing itself. Likewise, we do not have any idea how well it will recover, or whether it can actually even recover.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor... At the Defense Forces' command tower, if only I...

options: None of us expected to see Theresis there.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I never once imagined that Dr. Kal'tsit would one day be wounded this badly...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: She always solved all our problems like they were nothing. She gave us the best advice for every situation.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: She's Dr. Kal'tsit. I've never even seen her look tired!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But now...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I know. I will bear the responsibilities that are mine to bear. Rhodes Island's mission here is far from over.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But... I want to see Dr. Kal'tsit one more time. May I?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Even if it's just sitting there by her bed for a short while.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Rather than staying with the wounded, you two have more important work to do.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Closure wants you to know that she has finished analyzing the data from the command tower.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Clovisia is calling a meeting.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: We need to reevaluate the situation in Londinium.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Then please tell us what our step should be.
